subtopic: Pregnancy and postpartum emotional changes
passage:
Week 12: After the scan, Minakshi laughed all the way home, then cried in the auto because she would have to give up her dance classes. Avni, her sister, said, "You should only be happy!" Minakshi felt worse.
Week 20: Joy at the first kick, then panic at 3 am about labour, money and whether she would be any good at this. She was so tired she fell asleep at her desk.
Week 28: When Minakshi cried over a tiny sock and a hospital form in the same afternoon, Avni didn't correct her this time. She just sat down and said, "Both, huh?" Minakshi nodded and laughed through her tears. "Both."

qa.q: In which week did Minakshi feel the first kick?
qa.a: Week 20.

qa.q: What mix of feelings did Minakshi have after the first scan?
qa.a: She felt joyful, laughing all the way home, then sad and tearful about giving up her dance classes.

qa.q: What changed in how Avni responded, and why was it better?
qa.a: Avni stopped telling her to only be happy and simply accepted both feelings, which let Minakshi feel understood.

qa.q: How might Avni have meant "You should only be happy!"?
qa.a: As encouragement, without realising it made Minakshi feel her mixed feelings were wrong.

grounding: Shows a pregnant woman feeling joy, fear, tears and fatigue together, and those mixed feelings needing acceptance rather than correction.

subtopic: Pregnancy and postpartum emotional changes
passage: Varun, you look worried because your wife laughed and cried at breakfast. Listen to your old Dolma Ama. When I was carrying your father, in our tea-garden quarters above Darjeeling, I was twenty-four and I felt everything at once. I'd sing while plucking leaves, then sit down between the rows and weep for my mother, who had died the year before. I was proud, and frightened of the birth, and so tired I fell asleep standing at the stove. Your grandfather kept trying to fix it: "Don't cry, think happy things." That made me cry harder. It was the old midwife, Pasang, who said, "Joy and fear sit on the same stool, girl. Let them." After that I stopped fighting myself. So don't try to fix her, Varun. Sit with her.

qa.q: What did Dolma do while plucking leaves?
qa.a: She would sing.

qa.q: What was young Dolma feeling while pregnant?
qa.a: She felt proud and joyful, but also grieving for her mother, frightened of the birth and very tired.

qa.q: What turning point helped Dolma stop fighting her feelings?
qa.a: The midwife Pasang telling her that joy and fear can sit together and to let them.

qa.q: How did Dolma's husband respond to her tears, and why didn't it help?
qa.a: He kept trying to fix it by telling her to think happy things, which made her feel her tears were wrong.

grounding: Shows a pregnant woman feeling joy, grief, fear and fatigue together, and acceptance rather than correction helping her.

subtopic: Pregnancy and postpartum emotional changes
passage: They were moving flats in the middle of a Bengaluru downpour, boxes going soggy, the lift broken, and Minakshi, seven months pregnant, was supposed to be only directing. Instead she stood in the empty old kitchen and burst into tears. This was where she had found out she was pregnant; this was where she had danced with the test in her hand. She was thrilled about the bigger flat and the baby's room. And she was terrified, and exhausted, and grieving a kitchen. Thomas came in with a wet box. He almost said, "But the new place is better!" Then he didn't. He put the box down, stood beside her, and said, "It's a lot. All of it at once." Minakshi leaned on him and laughed and cried together. After a while she said, "Okay. Let's take the kettle last."

qa.q: What was broken during the move?
qa.a: The lift.

qa.q: What was Minakshi feeling in the old kitchen?
qa.a: She felt thrilled about the new flat but also terrified, exhausted and grieving the kitchen, all at once.

qa.q: What did Thomas do that helped?
qa.a: He held back from correcting her and simply named that it was a lot, accepting her mixed feelings.

qa.q: What might Thomas have been tempted to say, and why?
qa.a: "But the new place is better!", to cheer her up, though it would have brushed her feelings aside.

grounding: Shows a pregnant woman feeling joy, fear, sadness and tiredness at once, and a partner accepting the mixed feelings instead of correcting them.

subtopic: Pregnancy and postpartum emotional changes
passage:
Sunday, 1 am
Can't sleep. Latha is asleep with her hand on her belly, and I'm on the balcony pretending I'm fine.
Everyone says congratulations and you'll be a great dad. I nod. Inside it's: how do we manage on one salary for months, what if I turn out like my father, will I ever play Sunday cricket again. Then I feel guilty for even thinking about cricket.
I've been going quiet with Latha. Staying late at work. Last night she asked if I'm even happy about the baby. That scared me more than any of it.
Today I finally told Uday at the tea stall. He laughed, then got serious. "I felt exactly the same. Tell Latha. She'd rather know than guess."
Tomorrow at breakfast I'm telling her. All of it, even the cricket.
Jeevan

qa.q: Where did Jeevan finally tell Uday?
qa.a: At the tea stall.

qa.q: What is Jeevan feeling on the balcony?
qa.a: He feels proud yet anxious and pressured about money, turning out like his father and losing his freedom, and guilty for those thoughts.

qa.q: Why is telling Latha a good plan?
qa.a: Sharing the worries lets him support her instead of withdrawing, and she would rather know than guess.

qa.q: How might Latha be feeling about Jeevan's quietness?
qa.a: She seems hurt and unsure, even asking whether he is happy about the baby.

grounding: Shows an expectant father hiding worries about money, responsibility and freedom to seem strong, and choosing to share them instead of withdrawing.

subtopic: Pregnancy and postpartum emotional changes
passage: In the brass workshop at the edge of their village near Moradabad, Hrithik hammered harder than usual. Rehana was five months pregnant, the family was proud, and his mother had already sewn tiny kurtas. But at night he lay awake listening to the ceiling fan, adding numbers that never added up, thinking of the cricket team he would have to quit, wondering if he would shout like his own father. He came home later and later, ate in silence, and said "I'm fine" when Rehana asked. One evening she stood in the workshop doorway. "You're not fine. You're hiding from me." He put the hammer down. It all came out: the money, the freedom, the fear of becoming his father. Rehana sat on an upturned bucket. "I'm scared too. Let's be scared together, not separately." He walked home beside her for the first time in weeks.

qa.q: What had Hrithik's mother sewn?
qa.a: Tiny kurtas.

qa.q: What was Hrithik feeling at night?
qa.a: He felt anxious and pressured about money and freedom, and afraid of becoming like his father, even though the family was proud.

qa.q: What changed when Hrithik told Rehana everything?
qa.a: Sharing let them face the fears together instead of him withdrawing, so he walked home beside her.

qa.q: How had Rehana experienced his silence?
qa.a: She felt he was hiding from her, and she was scared too.

grounding: Shows an expectant father withdrawing under silent worries about money, freedom and becoming his father, and sharing them with his partner.

subtopic: Pregnancy and postpartum emotional changes
passage:
Day 3: Home from the hospital in Nagpur, Sakshi cried because the baby's cap was crooked, then because she had been happy a minute ago, then because she couldn't stop. She hadn't slept more than an hour at a stretch. Pranav hovered, frightened, asking what was wrong.
Day 5: Sakshi's mother moved into the spare room. Pranav took two of the night feeds with expressed milk so Sakshi could sleep. Her mother brought her hot food and sat with her. Sakshi still teared up at a lullaby, but she laughed at Pranav's attempts at nappies.
Day 12: The tears came less often. At the check-up Sakshi told the nurse about the crying days, and the nurse said it was common and to tell her if it kept going or got worse. That evening Sakshi sat on the balcony with the baby asleep on her chest and felt, mostly, like herself.

qa.q: Who moved into the spare room?
qa.a: Sakshi's mother.

qa.q: What was Sakshi feeling on day 3?
qa.a: She felt overwhelmed and unusually sensitive, crying at small things and unable to stop, with almost no sleep.

qa.q: What helped Sakshi by day 12?
qa.a: Rest while Pranav took night feeds, hot food and company from her mother, and telling the nurse, who asked to hear if it kept going.

qa.q: How did Pranav feel on day 3?
qa.a: He was frightened and unsure, hovering and asking what was wrong.

grounding: Shows a new mother crying easily and feeling overwhelmed in the first days after birth, and rest, food, reassurance and practical help easing it.

subtopic: Pregnancy and postpartum emotional changes
passage: Anand, you rang me at midnight because Priya cried all evening and you don't know what's wrong. Listen to your old Joseph Appachan. When your mother was born, in our house in Kottayam, your Ammachi, Mary, cried for days. She cried when the milk came in, cried when the neighbours visited, cried because the baby was beautiful. I was twenty-six and useless; I thought I had done something wrong. My own mother said, "Joseph, she's worn out and her body is changing back. Feed her, let her sleep, and hold the baby." So I did. I rocked your mother through the nights and brought Mary rice kanji and fish curry. My mother told her every morning, "You're doing well." Slowly Mary came back to herself. So bring Priya food, take the baby at night, and tell her she's doing well. And if the sadness stays or grows, take her to the doctor without delay.

qa.q: What did Joseph bring Mary?
qa.a: Rice kanji and fish curry.

qa.q: How did young Mary feel after the birth?
qa.a: She was overwhelmed and unusually tearful, crying at the milk coming in, at visitors and even at the baby's beauty.

qa.q: What turned things around for Mary?
qa.a: Joseph following his mother's advice: feeding Mary, letting her sleep, rocking the baby at night, and daily reassurance.

qa.q: How did young Joseph feel during those days?
qa.a: He felt useless and worried that he had done something wrong.

grounding: Shows a new mother tearful and overwhelmed in the days after birth, and food, rest, reassurance and practical help easing it.

subtopic: Pregnancy and postpartum emotional changes
passage: Five days after the birth, Gautam's company called him back to Pune for an audit, the power kept cutting out in the Jabalpur heat, and Tanvi was alone with the baby for the first time. By afternoon she was sitting on the floor beside the cradle, crying because the fan had stopped, because the baby had hiccups, because she didn't know why she was crying. She had slept perhaps three hours in two days. She almost didn't call anyone; she didn't want to seem weak. Then she rang her brother Tarun, who lived ten minutes away. He came with a bag of food and his wife, took the baby into the cooler room, and told Tanvi to sleep. When she woke at seven, there was dal and rice on the table and the baby was asleep. She still felt fragile. She phoned Gautam and said calmly, "I need you home by Friday."

qa.q: Why was Gautam called back to Pune?
qa.a: For an audit.

qa.q: What was Tanvi feeling on the floor beside the cradle?
qa.a: She was overwhelmed and tearful, crying at small things without knowing why, and exhausted.

qa.q: What made the difference that evening?
qa.a: Calling Tarun for practical help, so she could eat and sleep, and then asking Gautam to come home.

qa.q: How might Tarun feel on getting her call?
qa.a: He was probably concerned and glad she called, coming at once with food.

grounding: Shows a new mother crying easily and overwhelmed in the first days after birth, and food, sleep and practical help beginning to ease it.
